q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
~9 days (earnings release August 26, 2026; today is August 17, 2026). This is an imminent event with forward guidance that will be announced very shortly.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why
NVIDIA's own guidance from May 20, 2026 projects Q2 FY2027 revenue of $91.0 billion ± 2%, which translates to a range of $89.18B to $92.82B. The company typically provides reasonably accurate guidance (± 2% is a tight band), and they have strong visibility into their datacenter business over a ~3-month forward period.

The question asks for "forward guidance" from the Q2 FY2027 earnings release, which is ambiguous—it could mean:
1. Guidance for Q3 FY2027 (the October quarter), OR
2. Actual Q2 FY2027 results being reported, OR
3. The Q2 FY2027 guidance that was already provided in May

Given the phrasing "in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release" and the range provided (99.5-115.5B), I interpret this as asking for the Q3 FY2027 forward guidance that NVIDIA will announce when releasing Q2 results on August 26.

UBS forecasts Q3 FY2027 guidance of approximately $107-108 billion, based on steady Blackwell demand and a faster-than-expected Rubin ramp-up (500k GPU shipments/month). This provides third-party validation above the current guidance baseline.

The most likely outcome is guidance in the $105-110B range for Q3 FY2027.

## (c) What would push the value lower?
- Weaker-than-expected China demand or geopolitical restrictions limiting exports
- Slower-than-anticipated Rubin production ramp or customer adoption delays
- Inventory corrections at major customers (hyperscalers)
- Demand destruction from higher AI capex costs or slowing AI investment ROI
- Overall macro weakness affecting customer spending
- Conservative guidance bias (underpromise, overdeliver pattern)

## (d) What would push the value higher?
- Accelerated Rubin ramp exceeding UBS's 500k/month assumption
- Unexpectedly strong demand from new verticals (automotive, robotics, industrial AI)
- Potential China revenue recovery if geopolitical restrictions ease
- Blackwell demand stronger than expected, extending its revenue contribution
- Upward revision driven by better-than-expected Q2 actual results
- Aggressive guidance to signal confidence in product momentum

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values
From the research provided:
- NVIDIA's May 20, 2026 Q2 FY2027 guidance: $91.0B ± 2% ($89.18B–$92.82B)
- UBS Q3 FY2027 forecast: $107–108B

NVIDIA's typical guidance accuracy is tight (±2%), suggesting management has good visibility. The company rarely misses guidance significantly in either direction within a single quarter. Sequential growth from Q2 ($91B) to Q3 (UBS: $107–108B) would represent ~18–19% quarter-over-quarter growth, which is consistent with NVIDIA's historical acceleration patterns during strong product cycles (though 18% QoQ is on the high end for mature business).

---

## Reasoning on the range

The provided range is 99.5–115.5B. This appears centered roughly around $107–108B (the UBS forecast for Q3 FY2027 guidance). The range is wide enough to accommodate uncertainty around:
- Execution on Rubin ramp (500k/month is aggressive)
- China policy changes
- Customer demand volatility
- Inventory dynamics

Given:
1. UBS's research-backed estimate of $107–108B for Q3 guidance
2. The history of NVIDIA's tight guidance ± 2%
3. The ~9-day window before announcement (very short, limiting new data)
4. The upper bound of 115.5B seems to require exceptional upside (20%+ QoQ growth, Rubin execution better than UBS assumes)
5. The lower bound of 99.5B would imply demand disappointment or more conservative guidance

I estimate:
- **Median (50th): ~107.5B** — centered on UBS's midpoint, reflecting their detailed research and NVIDIA's operational visibility
- **Low (10th): ~101B** — assumes more conservative guidance or weaker-than-UBS demand expectations
- **High (90th): ~112B** — assumes accelerated Rubin ramp or stronger-than-expected sequential momentum

Low (10th percentile): 101000000000
Median (50th percentile): 107500000000
High (90th percentile): 112000000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026, covering the period that ended July 26, 2026 [aliteq.com](https://aliteq.com/nvidia-q2-fy27-earnings-preview-ubs-2026). For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's own guidance, provided on May 20, 2026, projects revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [barchart.com](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3449043/what-to-expect-from-nvidia-s-q2-2027-earnings-report). This guidance does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

UBS, however, predicts NVIDIA will report $94-95 billion for Q2 FY2027 and guide for an October-quarter (Q3 FY2027) revenue of roughly $107-108 billion. This is based on expectations of steady Blackwell demand and a faster-than-expected ramp-up of the next-gen Rubin platform, which UBS forecasts will reach 500,000 GPU shipments per month [aliteq.com](https://aliteq.com/nvidia-q2-fy27-earnings-preview-ubs-2026).
